/* Works out who should receive which reminder in a run as at $AsAtDate (BR-12, BR-15).
 * A customer receives the next stage only if still overdue and only one stage up from the last letter of the
 * current cycle - the cycle restarts when everything covered by the previous letters has been paid.
 * Returns an array of proposals keyed by debtorno. Customers who are not due a letter are included with
 * 'level' = 0 and a 'note' explaining why, so that credit control can see the whole picture. */
function ProposeDunningRun($AsAtDate, $Salesman = '', $Currency = '') {
	$Levels = GetDunningLevels();
	if (count($Levels) == 0) {
		return array();
	}
	$FirstLevel = reset($Levels);
	$MinDaysBetween = (int)CreditControlConfig('DunningMinDays', 14);

	$SQL = "SELECT DISTINCT debtorsmaster.debtorno,
					debtorsmaster.name,
					debtorsmaster.currcode,
					currencies.decimalplaces,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices
			FROM debtorsmaster
			INNER JOIN debtortrans
				ON debtorsmaster.debtorno=debtortrans.debtorno
			INNER JOIN paymentterms
				ON debtorsmaster.paymentterms=paymentterms.termsindicator
			INNER JOIN currencies
				ON debtorsmaster.currcode=currencies.currabrev
			INNER JOIN holdreasons
				ON debtorsmaster.holdreason=holdreasons.reasoncode
			WHERE ROUND(debtortrans.balance, currencies.decimalplaces) > 0
			AND DATEDIFF('" . $AsAtDate . "', " . DueDateSQL() . ") >= " . (int)$FirstLevel['daysoverdue'];
	if ($Salesman != '') {
		$SQL .= " AND debtorsmaster.debtorno IN (SELECT debtorno FROM custbranch WHERE salesman='" . $Salesman . "')";
	}
	if ($Currency != '') {
		$SQL .= " AND debtorsmaster.currcode='" . $Currency . "'";
	}
	$SQL .= SalesmanCustomerFilterSQL() . " ORDER BY debtorsmaster.debtorno";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);

	$Proposals = array();
	while ($Customer = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Items = GetOverdueItems($Customer['debtorno'], $AsAtDate, 1);
		$Proposal = $Customer;
		$Proposal['items'] = $Items;
		$Proposal['level'] = 0;
		$Proposal['note'] = '';
		$Proposal['emails'] = GetCustomerAccountsEmails($Customer['debtorno']);

		$BalResult = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $Customer['debtorno'] . "'");
		$BalRow = DB_fetch_row($BalResult);
		$Overdue = 0;
		$MaxDays = 0;
		$OldestDueDate = '';
		foreach ($Items as $Item) {
			$Overdue += $Item['balance'];
			$MaxDays = max($MaxDays, $Item['daysoverdue']);
			if ($OldestDueDate == '' or $Item['duedate'] < $OldestDueDate) {
				$OldestDueDate = $Item['duedate'];
			}
		}
		$Proposal['amount'] = round(min($Overdue, $BalRow[0]), $Customer['decimalplaces']);
		$Proposal['maxdays'] = $MaxDays;

		$Last = GetLastDunningLetter($Customer['debtorno']);
		$CurrentLevel = 0;
		if ($Last !== false and $OldestDueDate != '' and $Last['letterdate'] >= $OldestDueDate) {
			$CurrentLevel = $Last['levelno'];
		}
		$Proposal['lastletter'] = $Last;
		$Proposal['currentlevel'] = $CurrentLevel;

		$TargetLevel = 0;
		foreach ($Levels as $LevelNo => $Level) {
			if ($MaxDays >= $Level['daysoverdue']) {
				$TargetLevel = $LevelNo;
			}
		}
		/* step up one stage at a time */
		$NextLevel = 0;
		foreach ($Levels as $LevelNo => $Level) {
			if ($LevelNo > $CurrentLevel and $LevelNo <= $TargetLevel) {
				$NextLevel = $LevelNo;
				break;
			}
		}

		if (count($Items) == 0) {
			$Proposal['note'] = __('All overdue items are disputed');
		} elseif ($Proposal['amount'] <= 0) {
			$Proposal['note'] = __('Overdue items are covered by unallocated payments or credits');
		} elseif ($Last !== false and DateDiff(ConvertSQLDate($AsAtDate), ConvertSQLDate($Last['letterdate']), 'd') < $MinDaysBetween) {
			$Proposal['note'] = __('A reminder was sent on') . ' ' . ConvertSQLDate($Last['letterdate']);
		} elseif ($NextLevel == 0) {
			if ($CurrentLevel > 0 and $CurrentLevel == max(array_keys($Levels))) {
				$Proposal['note'] = __('Final notice already sent - credit control to decide on stop');
			} else {
				$Proposal['note'] = __('Not yet overdue enough for the next stage');
			}
		} else {
			$Proposal['level'] = $NextLevel;
			$Proposal['levelname'] = $Levels[$NextLevel]['levelname'];
		}
		$Proposals[$Customer['debtorno']] = $Proposal;
	}
	return $Proposals;
}

/* Fills in the letter wording for a proposal (BR-12, BR-17). Returns array(subject, body). */
function RenderDunningLetter($Level, $Proposal) {
	$Lines = '';
	foreach ($Proposal['items'] as $Item) {
		$Lines .= sprintf("%-22s %-10s %-12s %-12s %5s %15s\n",
						mb_substr(__($Item['typename']), 0, 22),
						$Item['transno'],
						ConvertSQLDate($Item['trandate']),
						ConvertSQLDate($Item['duedate']),
						$Item['daysoverdue'],
						locale_number_format($Item['balance'], $Proposal['decimalplaces']));
	}
	$Table = sprintf("%-22s %-10s %-12s %-12s %5s %15s\n", __('Transaction'), __('Number'), __('Date'), __('Due'), __('Days'), __('Outstanding') . ' ' . $Proposal['currcode'])
			. str_repeat('-', 82) . "\n" . $Lines;
	/* webERP stores text html encoded - the letters are plain text emails */
	$Replace = array('{CustomerName}' => html_entity_decode($Proposal['name'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'),
					'{CustomerCode}' => $Proposal['debtorno'],
					'{Currency}' => $Proposal['currcode'],
					'{OverdueAmount}' => locale_number_format($Proposal['amount'], $Proposal['decimalplaces']),
					'{InvoiceList}' => $Table,
					'{Date}' => ConvertSQLDate(date('Y-m-d')),
					'{CompanyName}' => html_entity_decode($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['coyname'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'),
					'{CompanyEmail}' => $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['email'],
					'{CompanyPhone}' => $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['telephone']);
	$Subject = strtr(html_entity_decode($Level['subject'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), $Replace);
	$Body = strtr(html_entity_decode($Level['bodytext'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), $Replace);
	if (mb_strpos($Level['bodytext'], '{InvoiceList}') === false) {
		$Body .= "\n\n" . $Table;
	}
	return array($Subject, $Body);
}

/* Records (and emails, if the customer has an accounts email address) a reminder letter (BR-13, BR-16).
 * Returns the letter id. */
function SendDunningLetter($Proposal, $Level) {
	list($Subject, $Body) = RenderDunningLetter($Level, $Proposal);
	$Method = (count($Proposal['emails']) > 0) ? 'E' : 'P';
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO dunningletters (debtorno,
										letterdate,
										levelno,
										currcode,
										amount,
										method,
										emailedto,
										subject,
										lettertext,
										sentby)
								VALUES ('" . $Proposal['debtorno'] . "',
										CURRENT_DATE,
										'" . $Level['levelno'] . "',
										'" . $Proposal['currcode'] . "',
										'" . $Proposal['amount'] . "',
										'" . $Method . "',
										'" . DB_escape_string(implode(', ', $Proposal['emails'])) . "',
										'" . DB_escape_string($Subject) . "',
										'" . DB_escape_string($Body) . "',
										'" . CreditControlUserID() . "')";
	$ErrMsg = __('The reminder letter could not be recorded because');
	DB_query($SQL, $ErrMsg, '', true);
	$LetterID = DB_Last_Insert_ID('dunningletters', 'letterid');
	foreach ($Proposal['items'] as $Item) {
		DB_query("INSERT INTO dunningletteritems (letterid, debtortransid, type, transno, duedate, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $LetterID . "',
							'" . $Item['id'] . "',
							'" . $Item['type'] . "',
							'" . $Item['transno'] . "',
							'" . $Item['duedate'] . "',
							'" . $Item['balance'] . "')", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	}
	LogCreditControlEvent($Proposal['debtorno'],
						'Reminder',
						$Level['levelname'] . ' - ' . ($Method == 'E' ? __('emailed to') . ' ' . implode(', ', $Proposal['emails']) : __('to be posted')),
						'',
						$Proposal['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Proposal['amount'], $Proposal['decimalplaces']),
						0,
						$LetterID);
	if ($Method == 'E') {
		$From = $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['coyname'] . ' <' . $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['email'] . '>';
		$Sent = SendEmailFromWebERP($From, $Proposal['emails'], $Subject, $Body, array(), true);
		if ($Sent !== true) {
			DB_query("UPDATE dunningletters SET method='F' WHERE letterid='" . $LetterID . "'", $ErrMsg, '', true);
		}
	}
	return $LetterID;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Month end interest and late payment fees
 * -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* Works out the interest and fees for the month ending $PeriodEndDate (Y-m-d) (BR-19 to BR-22).
 * Interest: simple interest at the annual rate on each overdue item (not on interest or fees, not on disputed
 * items) for the days of the month it was overdue.
 * Fee: one flat fee per customer per month, set in the home currency and converted at the current rate. */
function CalculateCreditCharges($PeriodEndDate) {
	$ChargeMonth = mb_substr($PeriodEndDate, 0, 7);
	$MonthStart = $ChargeMonth . '-01';
	$DaysInYear = date('L', strtotime($PeriodEndDate)) ? 366 : 365;
	$InterestRate = (float)CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestRate', 0);
	$InterestDays = (int)CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestDays', 30);
	$Fee = (float)CreditControlConfig('CreditLateFee', 0);
	$FeeDays = (int)CreditControlConfig('CreditFeeDays', 30);
	$MinDays = min($InterestRate > 0 ? $InterestDays : 99999, $Fee > 0 ? $FeeDays : 99999);
	if ($MinDays == 99999) {
		return array();
	}

	$SQL = "SELECT DISTINCT debtorsmaster.debtorno,
					debtorsmaster.name,
					debtorsmaster.currcode,
					debtorsmaster.interestexempt,
					debtorsmaster.feeexempt,
					currencies.rate,
					currencies.decimalplaces
			FROM debtorsmaster
			INNER JOIN debtortrans
				ON debtorsmaster.debtorno=debtortrans.debtorno
			INNER JOIN paymentterms
				ON debtorsmaster.paymentterms=paymentterms.termsindicator
			INNER JOIN currencies
				ON debtorsmaster.currcode=currencies.currabrev
			WHERE ROUND(debtortrans.balance, currencies.decimalplaces) > 0
			AND debtortrans.trandate <= '" . $PeriodEndDate . "'
			AND DATEDIFF('" . $PeriodEndDate . "', " . DueDateSQL() . ") >= " . $MinDays . "
			ORDER BY debtorsmaster.debtorno";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);

	$Charges = array();
	while ($Customer = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Charge = $Customer;
		$Charge['interest'] = 0;
		$Charge['fee'] = 0;
		$Charge['basis'] = 0;
		$Charge['note'] = '';

		$Charged = array();
		$ChargedResult = DB_query("SELECT chargetype FROM creditcharges
									WHERE debtorno='" . $Customer['debtorno'] . "'
									AND chargemonth='" . $ChargeMonth . "'");
		while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($ChargedResult)) {
			$Charged[$MyRow['chargetype']] = true;
		}

		$BalResult = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $Customer['debtorno'] . "'");
		$BalRow = DB_fetch_row($BalResult);

		$Items = GetOverdueItems($Customer['debtorno'], $PeriodEndDate, $MinDays, true);
		$Overdue = 0;
		$Interest = 0;
		$FeeDue = false;
		foreach ($Items as $Item) {
			$Overdue += $Item['balance'];
			if ($Item['daysoverdue'] >= $InterestDays) {
				/* days of this month the item was overdue */
				$OverdueFrom = max($Item['duedate'], date('Y-m-d', strtotime($MonthStart . ' -1 day')));
				$Days = (strtotime($PeriodEndDate) - strtotime($OverdueFrom)) / 86400;
				$Interest += $Item['balance'] * $InterestRate / 100 * round($Days) / $DaysInYear;
			}
			if ($Item['daysoverdue'] >= $FeeDays) {
				$FeeDue = true;
			}
		}
		/* unallocated payments and credits reduce what is overdue */
		if ($Overdue > 0 and $BalRow[0] < $Overdue) {
			$Factor = max($BalRow[0], 0) / $Overdue;
			$Interest = $Interest * $Factor;
			$Overdue = max($BalRow[0], 0);
			if ($Overdue <= 0) {
				$FeeDue = false;
			}
		}
		$Charge['basis'] = round($Overdue, $Customer['decimalplaces']);

		if ($Customer['interestexempt'] == 1) {
			$Charge['note'] .= __('Exempt from interest') . '. ';
		} elseif (isset($Charged['I'])) {
			$Charge['note'] .= __('Interest already charged for this month') . '. ';
		} elseif ($InterestRate > 0) {
			$Charge['interest'] = round($Interest, $Customer['decimalplaces']);
		}
		if ($Customer['feeexempt'] == 1) {
			$Charge['note'] .= __('Exempt from fees') . '. ';
		} elseif (isset($Charged['F'])) {
			$Charge['note'] .= __('Fee already charged for this month') . '. ';
		} elseif ($Fee > 0 and $FeeDue) {
			$Charge['fee'] = round($Fee * $Customer['rate'], $Customer['decimalplaces']);
		}
		if ($Charge['interest'] > 0 or $Charge['fee'] > 0 or $Charge['note'] != '') {
			$Charges[$Customer['debtorno']] = $Charge;
		}
	}
	return $Charges;
}

/* Posts an interest charge ('I') or late fee ('F') to the customer account and the general ledger (BR-21, BR-23).
 * Returns the transaction number. */
function PostCreditCharge($DebtorNo, $ChargeType, $Amount, $PeriodEndDate, $BasisAmount) {
	$ChargeMonth = mb_substr($PeriodEndDate, 0, 7);
	$Posting = GetCustomerPostingDetails($DebtorNo);
	$Type = ($ChargeType == 'I') ? CC_TYPE_INTEREST : CC_TYPE_FEE;
	$Account = ($ChargeType == 'I') ? CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestAct') : CreditControlConfig('CreditFeeAct');
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo($Type);
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(ConvertSQLDate($PeriodEndDate));
	$MonthName = MonthAndYearFromSQLDate($PeriodEndDate);
	if ($ChargeType == 'I') {
		$Text = __('Interest on overdue balance for') . ' ' . $MonthName . ' ' . __('at') . ' ' . locale_number_format(CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestRate'), 2) . '% ' . __('per annum');
	} else {
		$Text = __('Late payment fee for') . ' ' . $MonthName;
	}

	$DebtorTransID = InsertCreditControlDebtorTrans($Type, $TransNo, $DebtorNo, $Posting, $PeriodEndDate, $PeriodNo, $Text, $Amount, $Posting['rate'], $Text);

	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1) {
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans($Type, $TransNo, $PeriodEndDate, $PeriodNo, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'], $DebtorNo . ' - ' . $Text, $Amount / $Posting['rate']);
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans($Type, $TransNo, $PeriodEndDate, $PeriodNo, $Account, $DebtorNo . ' - ' . $Text, -$Amount / $Posting['rate']);
	}

	/* the unique key on debtorno, chargemonth, chargetype stops the same month being charged twice (BR-22) */
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO creditcharges (debtorno,
									chargemonth,
									chargetype,
									debtortransid,
									transtype,
									transno,
									amount,
									currcode,
									basisamount,
									rate,
									chargedate,
									chargedby)
							VALUES ('" . $DebtorNo . "',
									'" . $ChargeMonth . "',
									'" . $ChargeType . "',
									'" . $DebtorTransID . "',
									'" . $Type . "',
									'" . $TransNo . "',
									'" . $Amount . "',
									'" . $Posting['currcode'] . "',
									'" . $BasisAmount . "',
									'" . ($ChargeType == 'I' ? CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestRate') : 0) . "',
									NOW(),
									'" . CreditControlUserID() . "')";
	$ErrMsg = __('The charge could not be recorded - it may already have been charged for this month');
	DB_query($SQL, $ErrMsg, '', true);
	LogCreditControlEvent($DebtorNo, 'Charge', $Text, '', $Posting['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Amount, $Posting['decimalplaces']), $Type, $TransNo);
	return $TransNo;
}

/* Waives (reverses) a charge with a reason (BR-24). The waiver is a credit at the same exchange rate as the charge,
 * allocated against whatever is still outstanding on the charge. Returns the waiver transaction number. */
function WaiveCreditCharge($ChargeID, $Reason) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT creditcharges.*,
								debtortrans.rate,
								debtortrans.balance
						FROM creditcharges
						INNER JOIN debtortrans
							ON creditcharges.debtortransid=debtortrans.id
						WHERE creditcharges.chargeid='" . (int)$ChargeID . "'
						AND creditcharges.waived=0");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Charge = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Posting = GetCustomerPostingDetails($Charge['debtorno']);
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo(CC_TYPE_WAIVER);
	$TranDate = date('Y-m-d');
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']));
	$Account = ($Charge['chargetype'] == 'I') ? CreditControlConfig('CreditInterestAct') : CreditControlConfig('CreditFeeAct');
	$Text = __('Waiver of') . ' ' . ($Charge['chargetype'] == 'I' ? __('interest') : __('late payment fee')) . ' ' . $Charge['transno'] . ': ' . $Reason;
	$AllocAmount = min($Charge['amount'], max($Charge['balance'], 0));

	$CreditID = InsertCreditControlDebtorTrans(CC_TYPE_WAIVER, $TransNo, $Charge['debtorno'], $Posting, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, __('Waiver of') . ' ' . $Charge['transno'], -$Charge['amount'], $Charge['rate'], $Text, -$AllocAmount);
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1) {
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_WAIVER, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'], $Charge['debtorno'] . ' - ' . $Text, -$Charge['amount'] / $Charge['rate']);
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_WAIVER, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $Account, $Charge['debtorno'] . ' - ' . $Text, $Charge['amount'] / $Charge['rate']);
	}
	if ($AllocAmount > 0) {
		AllocateCreditControlCredit($CreditID, $Charge['rate'], $Charge['debtortransid'], $AllocAmount, CC_TYPE_WAIVER, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $Text);
	}
	$ErrMsg = __('The charge could not be marked as waived because');
	DB_query("UPDATE creditcharges
				SET waived=1,
					waivertransno='" . $TransNo . "',
					waivedby='" . CreditControlUserID() . "',
					waiveddate=NOW(),
					waivereason='" . DB_escape_string($Reason) . "'
				WHERE chargeid='" . (int)$ChargeID . "'", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	LogCreditControlEvent($Charge['debtorno'], 'Waiver', $Text, $Charge['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Charge['amount'], $Posting['decimalplaces']), '', CC_TYPE_WAIVER, $TransNo);
	return $TransNo;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Bad debt write-off
 * -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* Home currency value of an amount in the customer's currency at today's rate */
function HomeCurrencyValue($Amount, $CurrCode) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT rate FROM currencies WHERE currabrev='" . $CurrCode . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $Amount / $MyRow[0];
}

/* Records a write-off request. Write-offs with a home currency value above the approval limit wait for the Finance
 * Director (BR-26), the others are posted straight away. $Items is an array of debtortrans id => amount.
 * Returns the write-off id. */
function RequestWriteOff($DebtorNo, $Items, $Reason, $StopCustomer) {
	$Details = GetCustomerCreditDetails($DebtorNo);
	$Total = array_sum($Items);
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO writeoffs (debtorno,
									requestdate,
									requestedby,
									amount,
									currcode,
									homeamount,
									reason,
									stopcustomer,
									status)
							VALUES ('" . $DebtorNo . "',
									NOW(),
									'" . CreditControlUserID() . "',
									'" . $Total . "',
									'" . $Details['currcode'] . "',
									'" . HomeCurrencyValue($Total, $Details['currcode']) . "',
									'" . DB_escape_string($Reason) . "',
									'" . ($StopCustomer ? 1 : 0) . "',
									'P')";
	$ErrMsg = __('The write-off could not be recorded because');
	DB_query($SQL, $ErrMsg, '', true);
	$WriteOffID = DB_Last_Insert_ID('writeoffs', 'writeoffid');
	foreach ($Items as $DebtorTransID => $Amount) {
		DB_query("INSERT INTO writeoffitems (writeoffid, debtortransid, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $WriteOffID . "', '" . (int)$DebtorTransID . "', '" . $Amount . "')", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	}
	LogCreditControlEvent($DebtorNo, 'WriteOff', __('Write-off requested') . ': ' . $Reason, '', $Details['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Total, $Details['decimalplaces']), 0, $WriteOffID);
	if (HomeCurrencyValue($Total, $Details['currcode']) <= (float)CreditControlConfig('WriteOffApprovalLimit', 0)) {
		PostWriteOff($WriteOffID, false);
	}
	return $WriteOffID;
}

/* Checks the items of a write-off are still outstanding - they may have been paid since the request.
 * Returns an error message or '' */
function ValidateWriteOffItems($WriteOffID) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT writeoffitems.amount,
								debtortrans.balance,
								debtortrans.transno,
								systypes.typename
						FROM writeoffitems
						INNER JOIN debtortrans
							ON writeoffitems.debtortransid=debtortrans.id
						INNER JOIN systypes
							ON debtortrans.type=systypes.typeid
						WHERE writeoffitems.writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "'");
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		if ($MyRow['amount'] > $MyRow['balance'] + 0.005) {
			return __($MyRow['typename']) . ' ' . $MyRow['transno'] . ' ' . __('now only has') . ' ' . locale_number_format($MyRow['balance'], 2) . ' ' . __('outstanding - it has been paid or credited since the write-off was requested');
		}
	}
	return '';
}

/* Posts an approved write-off (BR-27): a credit to the customer at today's rate, allocated against the items
 * written off, with the bad debt charged to the bad debt account and the difference on exchange between the
 * invoice rates and today's rate posted to the exchange difference account. Puts the customer on stop if asked
 * (BR-28). */
function PostWriteOff($WriteOffID, $Approved) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT * FROM writeoffs WHERE writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "' AND status='P'");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$WriteOff = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Posting = GetCustomerPostingDetails($WriteOff['debtorno']);
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo(CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF);
	$TranDate = date('Y-m-d');
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']));
	$Text = __('Bad debt written off') . ': ' . $WriteOff['reason'];

	$CreditID = InsertCreditControlDebtorTrans(CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF, $TransNo, $WriteOff['debtorno'], $Posting, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, __('Write-off') . ' ' . $WriteOffID, -$WriteOff['amount'], $Posting['rate'], $Text, -$WriteOff['amount']);
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1) {
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, CreditControlConfig('BadDebtAct'), $WriteOff['debtorno'] . ' - ' . $Text, $WriteOff['amount'] / $Posting['rate']);
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'], $WriteOff['debtorno'] . ' - ' . $Text, -$WriteOff['amount'] / $Posting['rate']);
	}
	$TotalDiffOnExch = 0;
	$ItemsResult = DB_query("SELECT debtortransid, amount FROM writeoffitems WHERE writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "'");
	while ($Item = DB_fetch_array($ItemsResult)) {
		$TotalDiffOnExch += AllocateCreditControlCredit($CreditID, $Posting['rate'], $Item['debtortransid'], $Item['amount'], CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $WriteOff['debtorno'] . ' - ' . __('Write-off') . ' ' . $WriteOffID);
	}
	$ErrMsg = __('The write-off could not be updated because');
	DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET diffonexch='" . -$TotalDiffOnExch . "' WHERE id='" . $CreditID . "'", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	DB_query("UPDATE writeoffs
				SET status='A',
					transno='" . $TransNo . "',
					approvedby='" . ($Approved ? CreditControlUserID() : '') . "',
					approveddate=" . ($Approved ? "NOW()" : "NULL") . ",
					posteddate=NOW()
				WHERE writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "'", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	LogCreditControlEvent($WriteOff['debtorno'],
						'WriteOff',
						$Text . ($Approved ? ' - ' . __('approved by') . ' ' . CreditControlUserID() : ' - ' . __('within the approval limit')),
						'',
						$WriteOff['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($WriteOff['amount'], $Posting['decimalplaces']),
						CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF,
						$TransNo);
	if ($WriteOff['stopcustomer'] == 1) {
		SetCustomerCreditStatus($WriteOff['debtorno'], GetStopCreditStatus(), __('Automatically put on stop following bad debt write-off') . ' ' . $WriteOffID);
	}
	return $TransNo;
}

function RejectWriteOff($WriteOffID, $Reason) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT debtorno, amount, currcode FROM writeoffs WHERE writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "' AND status='P'");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$WriteOff = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$ErrMsg = __('The write-off could not be updated because');
	DB_query("UPDATE writeoffs
				SET status='R',
					approvedby='" . CreditControlUserID() . "',
					approveddate=NOW(),
					rejectreason='" . DB_escape_string($Reason) . "'
				WHERE writeoffid='" . (int)$WriteOffID . "'", $ErrMsg, '', true);
	LogCreditControlEvent($WriteOff['debtorno'], 'WriteOff', __('Write-off rejected') . ': ' . $Reason, $WriteOff['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($WriteOff['amount'], 2), '', 0, $WriteOffID);
	return true;
}

/* Reinstates part of a written-off debt when the customer pays it after all (open question 7): a debit to the
 * customer credited back to the bad debt account, against which the receipt is then allocated in the usual way. */
function PostBadDebtRecovery($DebtorNo, $Amount, $Reason) {
	$Posting = GetCustomerPostingDetails($DebtorNo);
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo(CC_TYPE_RECOVERY);
	$TranDate = date('Y-m-d');
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']));
	$Text = __('Bad debt recovered') . ': ' . $Reason;
	InsertCreditControlDebtorTrans(CC_TYPE_RECOVERY, $TransNo, $DebtorNo, $Posting, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, __('Bad debt recovered'), $Amount, $Posting['rate'], $Text);
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1) {
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_RECOVERY, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'], $DebtorNo . ' - ' . $Text, $Amount / $Posting['rate']);
		InsertCreditControlGLTrans(CC_TYPE_RECOVERY, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, CreditControlConfig('BadDebtAct'), $DebtorNo . ' - ' . $Text, -$Amount / $Posting['rate']);
	}
	LogCreditControlEvent($DebtorNo, 'Recovery', $Text, '', $Posting['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Amount, $Posting['decimalplaces']), CC_TYPE_RECOVERY, $TransNo);
	return $TransNo;
}

/* Checks the general ledger accounts that credit control posts to are set up - returns a list of problems */
function CreditControlGLSetupErrors($Accounts) {
	$Errors = array();
	$Names = array('CreditInterestAct' => __('Interest income account'),
					'CreditFeeAct' => __('Late payment fee income account'),
					'BadDebtAct' => __('Bad debt account'));
	foreach ($Accounts as $ConfName) {
		$Account = CreditControlConfig($ConfName, '');
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT accountcode FROM chartmaster WHERE accountcode='" . $Account . "'");
		if ($Account == '' or DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
			$Errors[] = $Names[$ConfName] . ' ' . __('is not set up in the credit control parameters');
		}
	}
	return $Errors;
}

input.content:
# Credit control – implementation notes

This change adds credit control to webERP, as asked for in `task/brd.md`: credit reviews, stop and watch, order credit holds on every order route, reminder letters, month-end interest and fees, bad debt write-offs, reports, the customer portal view, the month-end reconciliation with the GL, upgrade and fresh-install support, and the staff guide.

Nothing here has been run. There was no database or web server to run it against, so it has not been executed or tested. It still needs a full pass on a copy of the live database before go-live (see "What to test before go-live").

## How it fits into webERP

I reused the existing credit-status concept instead of adding a parallel one. A customer's credit status is still `debtorsmaster.holdreason`, and what a status *means* is still `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices`:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Normal |
| 1 | **On stop**: no orders, no dispatch or invoicing |
| 2 | **Watch**: trade, but warn and list orders for credit control |

The value 2 already existed in the code (SelectOrderItems, CounterSales and SpecialOrder warn on it, and upgrade 4.11.3 set it on the demo "Watch" code). It just could not be set from `CreditStatus.php`, and several screens treated it as "on hold". This change makes the three meanings explicit and uses them consistently.

New code lives in one library, `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`. Every page and route calls it, so the same rules apply whether an order comes from the sales office, the portal, EDI, a standing order or the API. None of its functions start or commit a transaction. The calling script wraps them, so the customer record, the credit-control records and the GL are always written together.

## What was built (new files)

| File | Purpose | Token |
|---|---|---|
| `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` | All credit-control logic: status/limit changes, reviews, order holds, overdue items, disputes, reminder proposals/letters, interest/fee calculation and posting, waivers, write-offs, recoveries, audit log | – |
| `CreditControlCustomer.php` | Per-customer workbench: status and reason, limit, balance, overdue, next review, last reminder; record a review; stop/watch/normal with a reason; exemptions; notes (e.g. "passed to collection agency"); mark/settle disputes; waive charges; review history; full audit history. Reps can view their own customers; changes need token 21 | 2 |
| `CreditControlReport.php` | BR-30: due/overdue for review, over limit (largest first), on stop, on watch; filter by rep and currency; home-currency totals | 2 |
| `CreditControlOrders.php` | Orders on credit hold, released with a reason; orders taken recently for customers on watch | 21 |
| `CreditControlParameters.php` | Finance settings: review months, interest rate/days/account, fee/days/account, bad debt account, write-off approval limit, minimum days between reminders, auto-stop status | 10 |
| `DunningLevels.php` | Reminder stages: number, days overdue, subject and wording with placeholders | 10 |
| `DunningRun.php` | Weekly run: prepare, review, untick (with reason, logged), send; lists letters to post | 21 |
| `PDFDunningLetter.php` | Prints a letter exactly as sent (for posting, staff and portal) | 1 |
| `CreditCharges.php` | Month-end interest and fees: prepare, review, untick, confirm and post | 21 |
| `BadDebtWriteOff.php` | Request write-off (all or part of items), approve/reject, record a recovery | 21 (approval needs 22) |
| `BadDebtWriteOffReport.php` | BR-29 | 3 |
| `CustomerCreditHistory.php` | Reminders and charges on an account. In the portal a customer only ever sees their own account | 1 |
| `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php` | Go-live load of the spreadsheet (status code, limit, review date, reason) with a test-run mode; every change is logged | 21 |
| `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html` | Staff guide for every item in BRD §4.1, plus the sales-staff note (BR-42/43) | – |
| `sql/updates/44.php` | Upgrade for existing installations | – |
| `install/sql/tables/*.sql` (9 new tables), `install/sql/data/holdreasons.sql`, `install/sql/data/dunninglevels.sql` | Fresh install | – |

New tables:

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `creditcontrollog` | Append-only audit trail (BR-32) |
| `creditreviews` | Insert-only (BR-03) |
| `debtortransdisputes` | Disputed items |
| `dunninglevels` | Reminder stages |
| `dunningletters`, `dunningletteritems` | Each letter, its exact text and the items it covered (BR-16) |
| `creditcharges` | Unique on customer + month + charge type, so a month cannot be charged twice (BR-22) |
| `writeoffs`, `writeoffitems` | Write-offs and the items they cover |

New columns:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `debtorsmaster` | `nextreviewdate`, `interestexempt`, `feeexempt` |
| `salesorders` | `credithold` (0 = not held / released, 1 = held because the customer is on stop, 2 = held because over the limit) |

New transaction types:

| Type | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Late Payment Interest | Separate, clearly described items on statements (statements print the type name) |
| 14 | Late Payment Fee | As above |
| 45 | Credit Charge Waiver | |
| 46 | Bad Debt Write-off | |
| 47 | Bad Debt Recovery | |

New security tokens:
- **21 Credit control**
- **22 Bad debt write-off approval**

There are also pseudo-scripts `CreditControlAuthority` and `WriteOffApproval`, the same pattern as `CostUpdate`, so the token needed can be changed in Page Security Settings.

## What else changed, and why

**Order routes.** BR-06 needs every route blocked, and BR-10 needs over-limit orders held.
- `SelectOrderItems.php`: shows the status banner with the reason when a customer is selected or an order is opened. Customers are never shown "watch". Fixed: customers on watch could not order in the portal (the check was `== 0`). On-stop customers in the portal get a clear "account on hold" message (BR-11). Re-applies holds as soon as an existing order's value changes. webERP writes changes to existing orders to the DB immediately, so without this a rep could add lines to a released order.
- `includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: warning for the new "hold" mode.
- `DeliveryDetails.php`: the server-side commit point. Refuses new orders for customers on stop (the stop may have been set while the cart was open), holds over-limit orders, re-checks modified orders and quotations turned into orders, and tells portal customers their order awaits approval.
- `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`: on stop, the recurrence is skipped and logged. Over-limit orders are held and **not** auto-invoiced (the auto-invoice path previously invoiced immediately).
- `EDIProcessOrders.php`: orders are kept but held, so the customer's order isn't lost, and the hold is noted in the notification email.
- `api/includes/api_salesorders.php`:
  - new error `CustomerOnHold` (1174) when a customer on stop places an order; the web shop shows it to the customer (BR-11);
  - over-limit orders are held as lines are added;
  - `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses held orders (`OrderOnCreditHold` 1175);
  - callers can no longer set `credithold` through the generic field mapping.
- `SpecialOrder.php`: over-limit hold.
- `CounterSales.php`: there is no approval step there, so the new "hold" mode acts as "prohibit".
- `Contracts.php`: in "hold" mode it only warns; the order is held when the contract quotation becomes an order.

**Dispatch and invoicing.**
- `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` refuses held orders, both when the order is opened and again at posting time.
- `GeneratePickingList.php` and `PDFPickingList.php` leave held orders off picking lists.
- `SelectSalesOrder.php` shows "Credit Hold" instead of the Invoice link.

**Who may change credit (BR-07).**
- `Customers.php`: the limit and status are read-only without token 21. New accounts opened by sales staff get the default limit and a normal status. With token 21, changes go through the logging functions, so who and why are recorded. Every new account gets a next review date (BR-02) and an "opened" history entry.
- `CreditStatus.php`:
  - now needs token 21;
  - offers Normal/Watch/Stop instead of a checkbox;
  - refuses to change the *meaning* of a code that customers have (that would silently stop or release every customer with that code).
- `Z_ImportDebtors.php` and `api/includes/api_customers.php`: limit and status changes are logged; new customers get a review date. The API's `ModifyCustomer` now requires token 21 to change credit fields. **This is a behaviour change for integrations.**
- `SystemParameters.php`: new `CheckCreditLimits` option 3, "Hold orders for credit control approval". Existing settings keep their behaviour, and the upgrade does not switch installations to 3. Our live system needs it set at go-live.

**Visibility (BR-09).** `SelectCustomer.php` shows the status banner and links to Credit Control and Reminders/Charges. `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` now say "ON WATCH" to staff instead of "ON HOLD".

**Portal security (BR-36).** `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` took the customer from `?CustomerID=`, so a customer logged in to the portal could view any other customer's account by editing the URL. They now always use the logged-in customer's own code. Customers also no longer see internal status descriptions such as "Watch" (open question 10). `index.php` adds "Reminders and Charges" to the customer menu.

**Reports.**
- `AgedDebtors.php` adds credit status, credit limit and last reminder (BR-31).
- `Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` was rewritten. It still read the `chartdetails` table, which no longer exists (replaced by `gltotals`), and it only counted invoices, credits and receipts, so it could not work. The new version:
  - reconciles every transaction type, including exchange differences, period by period;
  - lists each transaction where the ledger and the control account differ (BR-37/38, AC-08);
  - is moved to token 8 and added to the AR menu, because it is for the financial accountant.

**Manual.** `doc/Manual/ManualOutline.php` and `ManualCreditStatus.html` updated.

## Decisions on the BRD's open questions

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest basis | One simple annual rate set by Finance, applied per overdue item for the days of the month it was overdue, after the "days overdue" threshold. Not a statutory rate; the same rate for all currencies. Per-currency or statutory rates can be added later without changing the posting. |
| 2 | Late fee | One flat fee per customer per month, set in the home currency and converted at the day's rate (and rounded to the currency's decimals). |

| 4 | Stop after final reminder | Flag only. The run lists "final notice sent – credit control to decide on stop". Stopping a customer is a decision that needs a reason. |

| 7 | Written-off debt later paid | "Bad Debt Recovery" (type 47) reinstates the amount against the bad debt account; then the receipt is entered and allocated normally. Both the write-off and the recovery stay visible. |

| 10 | Watch visible in the portal? | No (the business's view). The portal shows only "on hold" when the customer is on stop. |
| 11 | Cover when both are away | Anyone holding token 21. Recommend the Finance Director's role has it; documented in the guide. |
| 12 | Branch groups sharing a limit | webERP already keeps the credit limit and balance at customer (debtor) level, shared by all its branches. Head-office groups across *separate customer accounts* are not supported; they would need a new grouping concept. |

- **Order holds are a flag on the order, not a new order status.** When a customer goes on stop, all their open orders are flagged (1). Release is per order, with a reason, by credit control (BR-06 "unless credit control releases them"). Taking a customer off stop does not mass-release orders: each is a credit decision. - **The credit limit check** reuses `GetCreditAvailable()`: balance plus uninvoiced open orders, against the limit.
  - A modified order is re-checked only if its value grew.
  - Turning a quotation into an order counts as a new order.
  - So changing a delivery address does not undo a release.
- **Standing orders for a customer on stop are skipped for that period**, not created on hold. Taking the customer off stop does not then release a backlog all at once. The skip is logged.

  - Nobody gets another letter within `DunningMinDays` (14 by default).

  - Charges post Dr debtors control / Cr income at the customer's current rate.
  - A waiver reverses at the *charge's* rate, so it has no exchange difference.
  - A write-off posts the bad debt at today's rate and allocates against the items.   - `EnsureGLEntriesBalance()` is called after each posting.

In webERP, what is already in the system is the truth, and the spreadsheet is loaded on top with `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php`. A fresh, non-demo install now gets three default status codes; it previously had none, which blocked creating customers. The demo data's "Watch" code (20) is set to mean Watch, and code 55 is renamed "On stop".

2. In Access Permissions Maintenance, give token 21 to the credit controllers' role and token 22 to the Finance Director's role.
3. In Credit Control Parameters, set the income and bad-debt GL accounts, the rate, the fee, the days overdue and the approval limit.
4. In System Parameters, set Check Credit Limits to "Hold orders for credit control approval".
5. Review the wording in Reminder Letter Stages (Legal to confirm).
6. Check every customer has an accounts contact flagged "send statement".
7. Load the spreadsheet with `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php`, test run first.

- **AC-01**: record a review that raises the limit with a six-month next review; the limit applies at once and the customer drops off the review list.
- **AC-02 / AC-11**: stop a customer, then try every route:
  - order entry and the portal (refused);
  - the API (error 1174);
  - EDI (order kept, held);
  - recurring orders (skipped);
  - invoicing and picking lists (held order refused and left off).
- **AC-04**: a watch customer's order is accepted with a warning and appears on Orders on Credit Hold.
- **AC-05**: an over-limit order is held until released.
- **AC-06**: reminder run with paid, disputed and escalating customers.
- **AC-07**: charges in a foreign currency, an exempt customer, and a second run for the same month (nobody charged twice).
- **AC-08**: write-off in a foreign currency, then the reconciliation agrees.
- **AC-09**: write-offs below and above the limit, and the approval refused to the requester.
- **AC-10**: rep and portal visibility.

# Credit control – implementation notes

This change adds credit control to webERP, as asked for in `task/brd.md`: credit reviews, stop and watch, order credit holds on every order route, reminder letters, month-end interest and fees, bad debt write-offs, reports, the customer portal view, the month-end reconciliation with the GL, upgrade and fresh-install support, and the staff guide.

Nothing here has been run. There was no database or web server to run it against, so it has not been executed or tested. It still needs a full pass on a copy of the live database before go-live (see "What to test before go-live").

## How it fits into webERP

I reused the existing credit-status concept instead of adding a parallel one. A customer's credit status is still `debtorsmaster.holdreason`, and what a status *means* is still `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices`:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Normal |
| 1 | **On stop**: no orders, no dispatch or invoicing |
| 2 | **Watch**: trade, but warn and list orders for credit control |

The value 2 already existed in the code (SelectOrderItems, CounterSales and SpecialOrder warn on it, and upgrade 4.11.3 set it on the demo "Watch" code). It just could not be set from `CreditStatus.php`, and several screens treated it as "on hold". This change makes the three meanings explicit and uses them consistently.

New code lives in one library, `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`. Every page and route calls it, so the same rules apply whether an order comes from the sales office, the portal, EDI, a standing order or the API. None of its functions start or commit a transaction. The calling script wraps them, so the customer record, the credit-control records and the GL are always written together.

## What was built (new files)

| File | Purpose | Token |
|---|---|---|
| `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` | All credit-control logic: status/limit changes, reviews, order holds, overdue items, disputes, reminder proposals/letters, interest/fee calculation and posting, waivers, write-offs, recoveries, audit log | – |
| `CreditControlCustomer.php` | Per-customer workbench: status and reason, limit, balance, overdue, next review, last reminder; record a review; stop/watch/normal with a reason; exemptions; notes (e.g. "passed to collection agency"); mark/settle disputes; waive charges; review history; full audit history. Reps can view their own customers; changes need token 21 | 2 |
| `CreditControlReport.php` | BR-30: due/overdue for review, over limit (largest first), on stop, on watch; filter by rep and currency; home-currency totals | 2 |
| `CreditControlOrders.php` | Orders on credit hold, released with a reason; orders taken recently for customers on watch | 21 |
| `CreditControlParameters.php` | Finance settings: review months, interest rate/days/account, fee/days/account, bad debt account, write-off approval limit, minimum days between reminders, auto-stop status | 10 |
| `DunningLevels.php` | Reminder stages: number, days overdue, subject and wording with placeholders | 10 |
| `DunningRun.php` | Weekly run: prepare, review, untick (with reason, logged), send; lists letters to post | 21 |
| `PDFDunningLetter.php` | Prints a letter exactly as sent (for posting, staff and portal) | 1 |
| `CreditCharges.php` | Month-end interest and fees: prepare, review, untick, confirm and post | 21 |
| `BadDebtWriteOff.php` | Request write-off (all or part of items), approve/reject, record a recovery | 21 (approval needs 22) |
| `BadDebtWriteOffReport.php` | BR-29 | 3 |
| `CustomerCreditHistory.php` | Reminders and charges on an account. In the portal a customer only ever sees their own account | 1 |
| `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php` | Go-live load of the spreadsheet (status code, limit, review date, reason) with a test-run mode; every change is logged | 21 |
| `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html` | Staff guide for every item in BRD §4.1, plus the sales-staff note (BR-42/43) | – |
| `sql/updates/44.php` | Upgrade for existing installations | – |
| `install/sql/tables/*.sql` (9 new tables), `install/sql/data/holdreasons.sql`, `install/sql/data/dunninglevels.sql` | Fresh install | – |

New tables:

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `creditcontrollog` | Append-only audit trail (BR-32) |
| `creditreviews` | Insert-only (BR-03) |
| `debtortransdisputes` | Disputed items |
| `dunninglevels` | Reminder stages |
| `dunningletters`, `dunningletteritems` | Each letter, its exact text and the items it covered (BR-16) |
| `creditcharges` | Unique on customer + month + charge type, so a month cannot be charged twice (BR-22) |
| `writeoffs`, `writeoffitems` | Write-offs and the items they cover |

New columns:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `debtorsmaster` | `nextreviewdate`, `interestexempt`, `feeexempt` |
| `salesorders` | `credithold` (0 = not held / released, 1 = held because the customer is on stop, 2 = held because over the limit) |

New transaction types:

| Type | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Late Payment Interest | Separate, clearly described items on statements (statements print the type name) |
| 14 | Late Payment Fee | As above |
| 45 | Credit Charge Waiver | |
| 46 | Bad Debt Write-off | |
| 47 | Bad Debt Recovery | |

New security tokens:
- **21 Credit control**
- **22 Bad debt write-off approval**

There are also pseudo-scripts `CreditControlAuthority` and `WriteOffApproval`, the same pattern as `CostUpdate`, so the token needed can be changed in Page Security Settings.

## What else changed, and why

**Order routes.** BR-06 needs every route blocked, and BR-10 needs over-limit orders held.
- `SelectOrderItems.php`: shows the status banner with the reason when a customer is selected or an order is opened. Customers are never shown "watch". Fixed: customers on watch could not order in the portal (the check was `== 0`). On-stop customers in the portal get a clear "account on hold" message (BR-11). Re-applies holds as soon as an existing order's value changes. webERP writes changes to existing orders to the DB immediately, so without this a rep could add lines to a released order.
- `includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: warning for the new "hold" mode.
- `DeliveryDetails.php`: the server-side commit point. Refuses new orders for customers on stop (the stop may have been set while the cart was open), holds over-limit orders, re-checks modified orders and quotations turned into orders, and tells portal customers their order awaits approval.
- `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`: on stop, the recurrence is skipped and logged. Over-limit orders are held and **not** auto-invoiced (the auto-invoice path previously invoiced immediately).
- `EDIProcessOrders.php`: orders are kept but held, so the customer's order isn't lost, and the hold is noted in the notification email.
- `api/includes/api_salesorders.php`:
  - new error `CustomerOnHold` (1174) when a customer on stop places an order; the web shop shows it to the customer (BR-11);
  - over-limit orders are held as lines are added;
  - `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses held orders (`OrderOnCreditHold` 1175);
  - callers can no longer set `credithold` through the generic field mapping.
- `SpecialOrder.php`: over-limit hold.
- `CounterSales.php`: there is no approval step there, so the new "hold" mode acts as "prohibit".
- `Contracts.php`: in "hold" mode it only warns; the order is held when the contract quotation becomes an order.

**Dispatch and invoicing.**
- `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` refuses held orders, both when the order is opened and again at posting time.
- `GeneratePickingList.php` and `PDFPickingList.php` leave held orders off picking lists.
- `SelectSalesOrder.php` shows "Credit Hold" instead of the Invoice link.

**Who may change credit (BR-07).**
- `Customers.php`: the limit and status are read-only without token 21. New accounts opened by sales staff get the default limit and a normal status. With token 21, changes go through the logging functions, so who and why are recorded. Every new account gets a next review date (BR-02) and an "opened" history entry.
- `CreditStatus.php`:
  - now needs token 21;
  - offers Normal/Watch/Stop instead of a checkbox;
  - refuses to change the *meaning* of a code that customers have (that would silently stop or release every customer with that code).
- `Z_ImportDebtors.php` and `api/includes/api_customers.php`: limit and status changes are logged; new customers get a review date. The API's `ModifyCustomer` now requires token 21 to change credit fields. **This is a behaviour change for integrations.**
- `SystemParameters.php`: new `CheckCreditLimits` option 3, "Hold orders for credit control approval". Existing settings keep their behaviour, and the upgrade does not switch installations to 3. Our live system needs it set at go-live.

**Visibility (BR-09).** `SelectCustomer.php` shows the status banner and links to Credit Control and Reminders/Charges. `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` now say "ON WATCH" to staff instead of "ON HOLD".

**Portal security (BR-36).** `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` took the customer from `?CustomerID=`, so a customer logged in to the portal could view any other customer's account by editing the URL. They now always use the logged-in customer's own code. Customers also no longer see internal status descriptions such as "Watch" (open question 10). `index.php` adds "Reminders and Charges" to the customer menu.

**Reports.**
- `AgedDebtors.php` adds credit status, credit limit and last reminder (BR-31).
- `Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` was rewritten. It still read the `chartdetails` table, which no longer exists (replaced by `gltotals`), and it only counted invoices, credits and receipts, so it could not work. The new version:
  - reconciles every transaction type, including exchange differences, period by period;
  - lists each transaction where the ledger and the control account differ (BR-37/38, AC-08);
  - is moved to token 8 and added to the AR menu, because it is for the financial accountant.

**Manual.** `doc/Manual/ManualOutline.php` and `ManualCreditStatus.html` updated.

## Decisions on the BRD's open questions

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest basis | One simple annual rate set by Finance, applied per overdue item for the days of the month it was overdue, after the "days overdue" threshold. Not a statutory rate; the same rate for all currencies. Per-currency or statutory rates can be added later without changing the posting. |
| 2 | Late fee | One flat fee per customer per month, set in the home currency and converted at the day's rate (and rounded to the currency's decimals). |
| 3 | Interest on interest/fees | No. Charges are excluded from the interest basis, and a customer who only owes earlier charges gets no new fee. Disputed items are excluded too (BR-18). |
| 4 | Stop after final reminder | Flag only. The run lists "final notice sent – credit control to decide on stop". Stopping a customer is a decision that needs a reason. |

| 6 | Write-off approval | The threshold is a Finance parameter, compared on the home-currency value. Default 0, meaning everything needs approval until Finance sets it. | 7 | Written-off debt later paid | "Bad Debt Recovery" (type 47) reinstates the amount against the bad debt account; then the receipt is entered and allocated normally. Both the write-off and the recovery stay visible. |
| 8 | Reps told the stop reason? | Yes, as user story 4 asks. The reason entered with the status change is shown wherever the customer is selected. |

| `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php` | Go-live load of the spreadsheet (status code, limit, review date, reason) with a test-run mode; every change is logged | 21 |
| `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html` | Staff guide for every item in BRD §4.1, plus the sales-staff note (BR-42/43) | – |
| `sql/updates/44.php` | Upgrade for existing installations | – |
| `install/sql/tables/*.sql` (9 new tables), `install/sql/data/holdreasons.sql`, `install/sql/data/dunninglevels.sql` | Fresh install | – |

New tables:

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `creditcontrollog` | Append-only audit trail (BR-32) |
| `creditreviews` | Insert-only (BR-03) |
| `debtortransdisputes` | Disputed items |
| `dunninglevels` | Reminder stages |
| `dunningletters`, `dunningletteritems` | Each letter, its exact text and the items it covered (BR-16) |
| `creditcharges` | Unique on customer + month + charge type, so a month cannot be charged twice (BR-22) |
| `writeoffs`, `writeoffitems` | Write-offs and the items they cover |

New columns:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `debtorsmaster` | `nextreviewdate`, `interestexempt`, `feeexempt` |
| `salesorders` | `credithold` (0 = not held / released, 1 = held because the customer is on stop, 2 = held because over the limit) |

New transaction types:

| Type | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Late Payment Interest | Separate, clearly described items on statements (statements print the type name) |
| 14 | Late Payment Fee | As above |
| 45 | Credit Charge Waiver | |
| 46 | Bad Debt Write-off | |
| 47 | Bad Debt Recovery | |

New security tokens:
- **21 Credit control**
- **22 Bad debt write-off approval**

There are also pseudo-scripts `CreditControlAuthority` and `WriteOffApproval`, the same pattern as `CostUpdate`, so the token needed can be changed in Page Security Settings.

## What else changed, and why

**Order routes.** BR-06 needs every route blocked, and BR-10 needs over-limit orders held.
- `SelectOrderItems.php`: shows the status banner with the reason when a customer is selected or an order is opened. Customers are never shown "watch". Fixed: customers on watch could not order in the portal (the check was `== 0`). On-stop customers in the portal get a clear "account on hold" message (BR-11). Re-applies holds as soon as an existing order's value changes. webERP writes changes to existing orders to the DB immediately, so without this a rep could add lines to a released order.
- `includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: warning for the new "hold" mode.
- `DeliveryDetails.php`: the server-side commit point. Refuses new orders for customers on stop (the stop may have been set while the cart was open), holds over-limit orders, re-checks modified orders and quotations turned into orders, and tells portal customers their order awaits approval.
- `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`: on stop, the recurrence is skipped and logged. Over-limit orders are held and **not** auto-invoiced (the auto-invoice path previously invoiced immediately).
- `EDIProcessOrders.php`: orders are kept but held, so the customer's order isn't lost, and the hold is noted in the notification email.
- `api/includes/api_salesorders.php`:
  - new error `CustomerOnHold` (1174) when a customer on stop places an order; the web shop shows it to the customer (BR-11);
  - over-limit orders are held as lines are added;
  - `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses held orders (`OrderOnCreditHold` 1175);
  - callers can no longer set `credithold` through the generic field mapping.
- `SpecialOrder.php`: over-limit hold.
- `CounterSales.php`: there is no approval step there, so the new "hold" mode acts as "prohibit".
- `Contracts.php`: in "hold" mode it only warns; the order is held when the contract quotation becomes an order.

**Dispatch and invoicing.**
- `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` refuses held orders, both when the order is opened and again at posting time.
- `GeneratePickingList.php` and `PDFPickingList.php` leave held orders off picking lists.
- `SelectSalesOrder.php` shows "Credit Hold" instead of the Invoice link.

**Who may change credit (BR-07).**
- `Customers.php`: the limit and status are read-only without token 21. New accounts opened by sales staff get the default limit and a normal status. With token 21, changes go through the logging functions, so who and why are recorded. Every new account gets a next review date (BR-02) and an "opened" history entry.
- `CreditStatus.php`:
  - now needs token 21;
  - offers Normal/Watch/Stop instead of a checkbox;
  - refuses to change the *meaning* of a code that customers have (that would silently stop or release every customer with that code).
- `Z_ImportDebtors.php` and `api/includes/api_customers.php`: limit and status changes are logged; new customers get a review date. The API's `ModifyCustomer` now requires token 21 to change credit fields. **This is a behaviour change for integrations.**
- `SystemParameters.php`: new `CheckCreditLimits` option 3, "Hold orders for credit control approval". Existing settings keep their behaviour, and the upgrade does not switch installations to 3. Our live system needs it set at go-live.

**Visibility (BR-09).** `SelectCustomer.php` shows the status banner and links to Credit Control and Reminders/Charges. `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` now say "ON WATCH" to staff instead of "ON HOLD".

**Portal security (BR-36).** `CustomerInquiry.php` and `CustomerAccount.php` took the customer from `?CustomerID=`, so a customer logged in to the portal could view any other customer's account by editing the URL. They now always use the logged-in customer's own code. Customers also no longer see internal status descriptions such as "Watch" (open question 10). `index.php` adds "Reminders and Charges" to the customer menu.

**Reports.**
- `AgedDebtors.php` adds credit status, credit limit and last reminder (BR-31).
- `Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` was rewritten. It still read the `chartdetails` table, which no longer exists (replaced by `gltotals`), and it only counted invoices, credits and receipts, so it could not work. The new version:
  - reconciles every transaction type, including exchange differences, period by period;
  - lists each transaction where the ledger and the control account differ (BR-37/38, AC-08);
  - is moved to token 8 and added to the AR menu, because it is for the financial accountant.

**Manual.** `doc/Manual/ManualOutline.php` and `ManualCreditStatus.html` updated.

## Decisions on the BRD's open questions

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest basis | One simple annual rate set by Finance, applied per overdue item for the days of the month it was overdue, after the "days overdue" threshold. Not a statutory rate; the same rate for all currencies. Per-currency or statutory rates can be added later without changing the posting. |
| 2 | Late fee | One flat fee per customer per month, set in the home currency and converted at the day's rate (and rounded to the currency's decimals). |
| 3 | Interest on interest/fees | No. Charges are excluded from the interest basis, and a customer who only owes earlier charges gets no new fee. Disputed items are excluded too (BR-18). |
| 4 | Stop after final reminder | Flag only. The run lists "final notice sent – credit control to decide on stop". Stopping a customer is a decision that needs a reason. |
| 5 | Over-limit web shop / standing orders | Held for approval, not rejected. The order is kept and nothing ships until credit control releases it. Customers *on stop* are rejected in the web shop with a message (BR-11); EDI orders for them are kept but held so the order isn't lost. |
| 6 | Write-off approval | The threshold is a Finance parameter, compared on the home-currency value. Default 0, meaning everything needs approval until Finance sets it. One approval level (token 22). The approver must be a different user from the requester. No separate Financial Accountant sign-off. |
| 7 | Written-off debt later paid | "Bad Debt Recovery" (type 47) reinstates the amount against the bad debt account; then the receipt is entered and allocated normally. Both the write-off and the recovery stay visible. |
| 8 | Reps told the stop reason? | Yes, as user story 4 asks. The reason entered with the status change is shown wherever the customer is selected. |
| 9 | Letters in other languages | Not in this release. Letters are in English; per-language wording would key off `debtorsmaster.language_id`. |
| 10 | Watch visible in the portal? | No (the business's view). The portal shows only "on hold" when the customer is on stop. |
| 11 | Cover when both are away | Anyone holding token 21. Recommend the Finance Director's role has it; documented in the guide. |
| 12 | Branch groups sharing a limit | webERP already keeps the credit limit and balance at customer (debtor) level, shared by all its branches. Head-office groups across *separate customer accounts* are not supported; they would need a new grouping concept. |

## Other decisions

- **Order holds are a flag on the order, not a new order status.** When a customer goes on stop, all their open orders are flagged (1). Release is per order, with a reason, by credit control (BR-06 "unless credit control releases them"). Taking a customer off stop does not mass-release orders: each is a credit decision. The upgrade flags open orders of customers already on stop, so nothing leaks through on day one.
- **The credit limit check** reuses `GetCreditAvailable()`: balance plus uninvoiced open orders, against the limit.
  - A modified order is re-checked only if its value grew.
  - Turning a quotation into an order counts as a new order.
  - So changing a delivery address does not undo a release.
- **Standing orders for a customer on stop are skipped for that period**, not created on hold. Taking the customer off stop does not then release a backlog all at once. The skip is logged.
- **Reminder escalation is one stage at a time.**
  - A customer first reaching the system at 95 days overdue gets the first letter, not the final notice.
  - The cycle restarts once everything covered by earlier letters is paid.
  - Nobody gets another letter within `DunningMinDays` (14 by default).
  - At send time the run is re-worked out; anyone who paid since preparing it is skipped (BR-15).
  - Letters are plain-text emails. Their exact text is stored, so the printed or portal copy is what was sent.
  - They go to customer contacts flagged "send statement" (the accounts contacts). There is no new field, because webERP already uses that flag for emailed statements.
- **GL and currency.**
  - Charges post Dr debtors control / Cr income at the customer's current rate.
  - A waiver reverses at the *charge's* rate, so it has no exchange difference.
  - A write-off posts the bad debt at today's rate and allocates against the items. The difference between the invoices' rates and today's goes to the sales exchange-difference account, using the same convention as `CustomerAllocations.php`. The debtors control account is therefore reduced by exactly the carrying value (BR-27 "including any currency difference").
  - No tax is charged on interest or fees.
  - `EnsureGLEntriesBalance()` is called after each posting.
- **Charges are dated the month end** and post to that period. Run them before the period is closed.
- **Roles.** The upgrade gives tokens 21 and 22 to the System Administrator role only. I did not create new roles: webERP does not copy menus to roles created after install. The admin ticks token 21 on the credit controllers' role and 22 on the Finance Director's role in Access Permissions Maintenance.
- **Existing customers keep their current status and limit**; nothing is reset to "normal". BR-40's "start as normal" describes the spreadsheet world. In webERP, what is already in the system is the truth, and the spreadsheet is loaded on top with `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php`. Every existing customer gets a next review date 12 months out, which Finance can overwrite with the import.
- **The upgrade creates "On stop" and "Watch" status codes** if none exist, and sets `CreditStopReason`. A fresh, non-demo install now gets three default status codes; it previously had none, which blocked creating customers. The demo data's "Watch" code (20) is set to mean Watch, and code 55 is renamed "On stop".
- **Free text from forms is un-escaped with `CCInput()`.** `session.php` already SQL-escapes and HTML-encodes all `$_POST`/`$_GET`, and the library escapes what it stores, because it also stores system-generated text. Without the un-escape, notes would be stored double-escaped.

## Installation

1. Deploy the files. Logging in runs DB update 44, which creates the tables, columns, types, tokens, menu items, default stages and config.
2. In Access Permissions Maintenance, give token 21 to the credit controllers' role and token 22 to the Finance Director's role.
3. In Credit Control Parameters, set the income and bad-debt GL accounts, the rate, the fee, the days overdue and the approval limit.
4. In System Parameters, set Check Credit Limits to "Hold orders for credit control approval".
5. Review the wording in Reminder Letter Stages (Legal to confirm).
6. Check every customer has an accounts contact flagged "send statement".
7. Load the spreadsheet with `Z_ImportCreditStatus.php`, test run first.

## What to test before go-live

Nothing has been run, so every acceptance criterion needs testing:

- **AC-01**: record a review that raises the limit with a six-month next review; the limit applies at once and the customer drops off the review list.
- **AC-02 / AC-11**: stop a customer, then try every route:
  - order entry and the portal (refused);
  - the API (error 1174);
  - EDI (order kept, held);
  - recurring orders (skipped);
  - invoicing and picking lists (held order refused and left off).
- **AC-04**: a watch customer's order is accepted with a warning and appears on Orders on Credit Hold.
- **AC-05**: an over-limit order is held until released.
- **AC-06**: reminder run with paid, disputed and escalating customers.
- **AC-07**: charges in a foreign currency, an exempt customer, and a second run for the same month (nobody charged twice).
- **AC-08**: write-off in a foreign currency, then the reconciliation agrees.
- **AC-09**: write-offs below and above the limit, and the approval refused to the requester.
- **AC-10**: rep and portal visibility.

## Not done / known limitations

- Per-language letter wording; statutory or per-currency interest rates; credit-insurance and agency feeds (out of scope).
- Interest uses current item balances as at the month end chosen. Running charges well after month end, after payments, gives a lower figure than a strict historic balance would.
- `sql/demo.sql` (the legacy root dump used by `Z_MakeNewCompany`) was not updated; `install/sql/demo.sql` was.
- The portal fix covers the account pages this feature relies on (`CustomerInquiry.php`, `CustomerAccount.php`, and the new pages). Other customer-accessible scripts (e.g. printing transactions) were not audited.
- Translations (`locale/*`) of the new strings and the manual are not provided.

content.text:
I've built the whole credit control feature, but none of it has been run — there was no database or web server here, so it is untested. It needs a full pass of the BRD's acceptance criteria (AC-01 to AC-11) on a copy of the live database before go-live; `NOTES.md` lists what to try.

**How it fits in.** I reused webERP's existing customer credit status codes, which already had a little-used "watch" value, rather than adding a parallel system. Each code now means Normal, Watch or On stop. All the rules live in one shared library, `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`, and every way an order can arrive goes through it: sales office, customer portal, web shop (API), EDI, standing orders and special orders.

**New screens:**
- **Customer credit control:**
  - credit reviews, putting customers on stop or watch with a reason;
  - marking disputed invoices, exemptions from interest and fees, and waiving charges;
  - notes, and the full history for the auditors.
- **Orders held for credit control:** release with a reason, plus the list of orders taken for customers on watch.
- **Weekly reminder letter run:** preview, leave customers out with a reason, then email; customers with no email are listed for posting.
- **Month-end interest and fees:** preview and confirm. A month can never be charged twice to the same customer.
- **Bad debt write-off:** with approval above Finance's limit by someone other than the requester, and a way to reinstate a written-off debt that is later paid.
- **Credit control report and write-off report.**
- **Reminders and charges page in the customer portal.**
- **Finance settings and reminder letter wording.**
- **Go-live loader** for the spreadsheet stop list, limits and review dates.

**Existing code I had to change:**
- **Order entry and invoicing:** customers on stop are refused at order entry. Orders that would go over the credit limit are held until credit control releases them. Held orders can't be invoiced and are left off picking lists.
- **Standing orders:** a standing order for a customer on stop is skipped, rather than created and held. Previously an auto-invoiced standing order would have been invoiced straight away.
- **Customer maintenance and the customer API:** credit limits and status can only be changed with the new credit-control permission, and every change is logged with who and why. This is a behaviour change for any integration that sets credit limits through the API.
- **Portal security hole:** a customer logged into the portal could open any other customer's account by editing the URL. I fixed this on the account pages; other customer-facing pages (e.g. printing transactions) were not checked.
- **Month-end reconciliation:** the existing check between customer balances and the general ledger read a table that no longer exists, so it could not work. I rewrote it, and it now lists each transaction that doesn't agree.
- **Other changes:**
  - the aged debtors report now shows credit status, limit and last reminder;
  - the staff guide has a new credit control chapter, including the note for sales staff.

**Open questions — my decisions:**

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interest | One simple annual rate for all currencies, not a statutory rate |
| 2 | Late fee | One flat fee per customer per month, set in home currency |
| 3 | Interest on interest/fees | No |
| 4 | Stop after final notice | Flagged for the credit controller to decide, not automatic |
| 5 | Over-limit web shop / standing orders | Held for approval, not rejected |
| 6 | Write-off approval | One approver, threshold set by Finance (default 0, so everything needs approval until set); no separate accountant sign-off |
| 7 | Written-off debt later paid | Shown as a "bad debt recovery", then the receipt is allocated normally |
| 8 | Reps see the stop reason? | Yes |
| 9 | Other languages | English only for now |
| 10 | Watch visible in portal? | No |
| 11 | Cover when both are away | Anyone given the credit-control permission; I recommend the Finance Director |
| 12 | Branch groups sharing a limit | Branches of one customer share its limit; groups across separate accounts aren't supported |

**Things you need to do at go-live** (the upgrade deliberately doesn't change these for other installations):
- Give the credit controllers' role and the Finance Director's role the new permissions; the upgrade only gives them to the System Administrator.
- Switch "Check Credit Limits" to "Hold orders for credit control approval".
- Have Finance set the interest, fee and bad debt general ledger accounts, the rate, the fee and the approval limit.

Existing customers keep their current status and limit; the spreadsheet is then loaded on top with the import screen.

Everything above is written up in `NOTES.md` at the repository root, including the full file list and the installation steps.
